titlePolicy.basis: User-selected original topic first; use the topic-faithful revisions from the immediately preceding comparison as the recommended draft. Confirm against full lesson and selected footage before TTS.
titlePolicy.finalizeAfter: Read the full relevant lesson narration and visuals, preserve the teaching backbone, confirm actual independent footage, and verify that the resulting script answers the title promise.

translationNotes.note: Assigning Animations concerns communicating a director's intended character movements to the art team through production instructions. It is not a lesson about assigning animations or switching states at runtime. The browser's localized title '애니메이션 할당' is retained only in the raw observation.
Follow-through here includes the recovery period following an attack or other animation. Preserve the role of the post-action movement instead of reducing the lesson to a generic attack-speed tip.
Flipped Animation concerns directional presentation, including keeping Kirby's face or Mario's belly visible when facing the opposing direction. Do not recast it as a general rotation tutorial.

The official description addresses why simply assigning attack collision to an animation as-is often fails and why animators should consider attack collision. The draft title is not a claim that a particular game has a verified hit-detection bug.

visualPolicy.visualIntent: Light neutral square grid, grounded floor/reference line, sparse axis markers, fixed readable character scale and shared A/B framing. Adapt the submitted layout without reusing its characters or pixels.
visualPolicy.firstChoice: Test a short independently sourced FHD gameplay clip for character separation and composite it onto our grid.
visualPolicy.fallback: If separation damages the demonstrated motion, prefer rights-verified independent FHD animation-tool or native training-grid recordings. Use our licensed Unity animation preview only as a separately labelled explanation.
visualPolicy.sourceSeparation: Finished reference lessons and character extractions from them remain research-only and must never enter the production cut list.
visualPolicy.disclosure: A composited background is an editorial motion study, not proof of access to an original game editor. Distinguish original game/tool recording, background-separated composite and our Unity demonstration.
visualPolicy.ratio: Retain the ordinary game-content 60:40 contract unless the user changes it. Tool recordings have their own source kind; self-authored Unity remains explanation. Never pad or relabel footage to meet a ratio.
